rationale: The workflow already caches Ruby dependencies via ruby/setup-ruby with bundler-cache: true, which is the equivalent of the P-LIT-GHA-CACHE dependency-cache optimization; adding a separate actions/cache step would be redundant and matches the pattern contraindication that an equivalent cache already exists. P-LIT-FAIL-FAST (fail-fast: true) is contraindicated because every Ruby-version matrix outcome is required to preserve build/test coverage, so cancelling remaining matrix jobs would hide required results. P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE lacks an approved monitored pause/resume policy, and the weekly schedule may be a mandatory periodic check; recent history shows only two consecutive schedule failures with no evidenced pause policy. Other patterns (change filtering, test selection, custom timeouts) would reduce coverage or lack representative history/prerequisites. No supported, coverage-preserving optimization applies.
